lesson.title: Lists
lesson.driving_question: How can one variable hold a growing collection of items?
lesson.primary_concept_family: Lists store ordered collections that a program can change.
lesson.concept_budget: One collection family and one mutation method; do not iterate or count yet.
misconceptions: A list needs square brackets and commas between its items.
append() adds one item to the end of the list.
The list variable keeps the changed collection after append().
append() needs parentheses and the item is passed inside them.
lesson.progression_note: A fixed list becomes a changing list when the learner appends one user choice. Lesson 11 will read the collection with a loop and len().
code_expectations: one append() call per added item

shared_program.code:
item = input("Pack one item: " )
packing_list = ["water", "map"]
packing_list.append(item)
print("Packing list:", packing_list)

primm.prompt: Recall: What does a variable store? How does input() get text? What do square brackets show?
Without running the code, use the input 'torch'. Predict the list before and after append(), then predict the final display. Explain your prediction to a partner.
Run the supplied file with 'torch'. Compare the displayed list with your prediction and explain one match or mismatch.

questions: If you enter compass, what exact list is printed?
Why does append(item) add one item instead of joining the characters of item separately?
Which line adds the new item to packing_list?
Why is the new item placed at the end rather than at position 0?

primm.prompt: Add "snacks" as the third item in [packing_list]. Keep the input and append() lines so the user's item is added after it. Test the input "coat"; display "Packing list: ['water', 'map', 'snacks', 'coat']".
The user should add two items in total. Ask for a second item, append it, then show all four items in the final packing list.

Store "film" and "popcorn" in a list called [movie_night]. Ask for another item and store it in [item]. Append [item] to [movie_night], then display "Movie-night checklist:" followed by the list. Test "tickets"; display "Movie-night checklist: ['film', 'popcorn', 'tickets']".
Repair the undefined item used in append(), then run the corrected packing-list program.

blocks.definition: An ordered collection of items written between square brackets. Items are separated with commas.
The square-bracket code which creates a list and gives it its starting items.
Adds one item to the end of a list. The item goes inside the parentheses.
A list can hold its original items and a new item after the program calls append().
Create a starting list, ask for one more item, append the answer and display the changed list.
blocks.example:
item = input("Pack one item: " )
packing_list = ["water", "map"]
packing_list.append(item)
print("Packing list:", packing_list)
